name: Gott and Li's Self-Creating Universe
description: De Sitter space with each event identified with its images under a boost, proposed by J. Richard Gott and Li-Xin Li in 1998. It begins in a region of closed timelike curves of finite spacetime volume, with no earliest event, and a Cauchy horizon separates that region from an inflating universe in which nothing returns to its own past.
convention: We keep factors of $c$ explicit. The Ricci tensor is the standard contraction, $R_{\mu\nu} = R^\alpha{}_{\mu\alpha\nu}$.
history: J. Richard Gott and Li-Xin Li compared the beginning of time to the Earth, which has a southernmost point and no easternmost one [gott1998]. The two accounts of the beginning of the universe that they counted the best so far, Alexander Vilenkin's tunnelling from nothing of 1982 and the no boundary proposal of James Hartle and Stephen Hawking a year later, gave time a south pole, a first moment with nothing before it [vilenkin1982, hartle1983, gott1998]. Gott and Li, at Princeton, wanted a beginning like the east, where a traveller can keep going round and round, and in a paper dated 29 December 1997 they asked "whether there is anything in the laws of physics that would prevent the Universe from creating itself" [gott1998]. General relativity has room for the idea, since it allows closed timelike curves, paths through spacetime that return to their own starting event [gott1998]. With a region of such curves at the start, every event has events before it, and yet the universe has not lasted forever [gott1998].¶Inflation had moved the first moment back without removing it [gott1998]. By a theorem of 1994 due to Arvind Borde and Vilenkin, "a physically reasonable spacetime that is eternally inflating to the future must possess an initial singularity" [bordevilenkin1994]. Gott's own picture, from 1982, had our universe as one of the bubbles that keep forming in an inflating de Sitter space, each bubble an open universe inside [gott1982, gott1998]. Edward Farhi, Alan Guth, and Jemal Guven had worked out how such a universe might produce new ones: a small bubble of inflating vacuum made inside it usually collapses into a black hole, and occasionally one tunnels into a new inflating universe on the far side of the hole [farhi1990, gott1998]. If one of those babies is the very de Sitter space that the bubbles came from, then, in Gott and Li's words, "the Universe is its own mother" [gott1998].¶Their simplest example is de Sitter space rolled up along a boost [gott1998]. De Sitter space is a hyperboloid in a flat spacetime of five dimensions, $W^2 + X^2 + Y^2 + Z^2 - V^2 = r_0^2$ with $r_0 = \sqrt{3/\Lambda}$, and a boost in the plane of $V$ and $W$ slides the hyperboloid along itself [gott1998]. Gott and Li declared every event and its boosted image to be one event, which is what Charles Misner had done to flat spacetime in 1967 [gott1998, misner1967]. For the observer at the centre of a static patch the boost is a step of $\beta/c$ in the patch's own time $t$, so time there is a circle: an observer who waits long enough at a fixed radius $r$ arrives back at the starting moment [gott1998]. This looping region holds a finite volume of spacetime, $\tfrac{4}{3}\pi\beta r_0^3$, and ends at the horizon $r = r_0$, which is made of light rays that close on themselves [gott1998]. Beyond the horizon the same step is taken along a direction of space, round a circle that starts at zero size and grows as $\sinh(c\tau/r_0)$, and from there on the universe inflates and nothing returns to its own past [gott1998].¶Would the vacuum let such a horizon stand? William Hiscock and Deborah Konkowski had calculated the stress energy of a quantum field on Misner space and found it growing without bound toward the horizon, and Hawking's chronology protection conjecture of 1992 rests on results of that kind: the laws of physics do not allow closed timelike curves to appear [hiscock1982, hawking1992, li1998]. Li and Gott's answer, sent to the journal in September 1997, was another vacuum for Misner space, Rindler's, whose stress energy is zero everywhere when the boost has rapidity $2\pi$ [li1998]. Misner space and the de Sitter universe have the same light cones, so the state carries over, and its stress energy stays finite on the horizon only for $\beta = 2\pi r_0$ [gott1998]. In units with $\hbar = c = k_B = 1$ it is then $-g_{ab}/(960\pi^2r_0^4)$, the value in de Sitter space with nothing identified, and the same $\beta$ leaves no conical point on the sphere of four dimensions that is the Euclidean form of the space [gott1998]. A particle detector at rest in the looping region registers nothing, and one beyond the horizon feels the Gibbons-Hawking temperature $1/2\pi r_0$ of ordinary de Sitter space [gott1998].¶A wave sent out near such a horizon meets its own earlier laps again and again [gott1998]. By Hawking's argument, waves pile up on a horizon that has the closed curves in its future, each lap bluer than the last, until they destroy it [hawking1992, gott1998]. Gott and Li's horizon has the closed curves in its past, where each lap is redder, and they found the fields consistent only if every wave in the looping region and in the inflating one travels forward in time, the retarded waves of ordinary experience [gott1998]. So the loop at the beginning fixes an arrow of time for everything after it [gott1998]. The looping region itself has to be empty, a cold vacuum with no particles and no bubbles, and for $\beta = 2\pi r_0$ a bubble born later than $0.086\,r_0/c$ after the horizon never runs into its own image [gott1998]. The universe that results has no earliest event and is still geodesically incomplete to the past, "not a property we should have thought desirable" [gott1998].¶By September 1997 Hawking no longer counted on the stress energy: with Michael Cassidy he granted that "back reaction does not enforce chronology protection" [cassidy1998]. The two proposed another guard, the entropy of a scalar field on the product of de Sitter space of three dimensions and a circle, which runs to minus infinity as closed timelike curves are about to appear, so that the number of available quantum states tends to zero [cassidy1998]. Gott and Li replied that a state of low entropy on the horizon is what the early universe needs in any case [gott1998]. On the conjecture itself they wrote: "Perhaps a conclusion on the chronology protection conjecture can only be reached after we have a quantum theory of gravity" [gott1998]. Hiscock objected in 2000 to the fine tuning: the Rindler vacuum is harmless for a single value of the boost and for a free field coupled conformally to the curvature [hiscock2000]. For a field with any other coupling, or one that interacts with itself, he found on Misner space that "the vacuum stress-energy always diverges on the chronology horizons" [hiscock2000].

related.text: The same hyperboloid with nothing identified. Gott and Li's universe is de Sitter space with each event and its images under a boost counted as one event [gott1998].
Flat spacetime identified under the same boost. A conformal map relates Misner space to Gott and Li's universe, and they used it to carry Li and Gott's vacuum across [gott1998, li1998].

De Sitter space with events identified under the antipodal map of its hyperboloid, where Gott and Li identify them under a boost. The antipodal map makes no closed timelike curve, and it removes the global direction of time [parikh2003].
Gott's earlier spacetime with closed timelike curves, two cosmic strings passing at high speed [gott1991]. Away from the strings it is flat spacetime identified under a boost and a shift [grant1993].
Beyond the Cauchy horizon each moment of constant $\tau$ is a circle times a sphere, and Gott and Li call the region a type of Kantowski-Sachs universe [gott1998].
The bubbles that end inflation. Gott and Li have them forming in the inflating region beyond the Cauchy horizon, each an open universe inside [gott1998, gott1982].
Any spacetime with closed timelike curves has the Malament-Hogarth property, as John Byron Manchak observed in 2010 [manchak2010].
The beginning Gott and Li set out to replace: half a four sphere joined to de Sitter's waist, whose south pole they called the earliest point in Euclidean time [gott1998, vilenkin1982].

coordinates.name: Static

parameters.description: De Sitter radius, a length, fixed by the cosmological constant $\Lambda$ through $r_0 = \sqrt{3/\Lambda}$; the Cauchy horizon sits at $r = r_0$
Period of $ct$, a length; each event is identified with its images under a boost of rapidity $\beta/r_0$

coordinates.convention: We use coordinates $(t, r, \theta, \phi)$, with $t$ carrying dimensions of time and periodic with period $\beta/c$, and $r$ the areal radius. We take components in the chart $x^0 = ct$, and a dot in the geodesic equations is a derivative with respect to an affine parameter, so $\dot{t}$ means $d(ct)/d\lambda$.
geodesics: \ddot{r} - \dfrac{r\left(r_0 + r\right)\left(r_0 - r\right)}{r_0^4}\dot{t}^2 + \dfrac{r}{\left(r_0 + r\right)\left(r_0 - r\right)}\dot{r}^2 - \dfrac{r\left(r_0 + r\right)\left(r_0 - r\right)}{r_0^2}\dot{\theta}^2 - \dfrac{r\left(r_0 + r\right)\left(r_0 - r\right)\sin^2\theta}{r_0^2}\dot{\phi}^2 = 0

coordinates.name: Kantowski-Sachs

parameters.description: De Sitter radius, a length, fixed by the cosmological constant $\Lambda$ through $r_0 = \sqrt{3/\Lambda}$; the spheres of constant $\tau$ and $l$ have radius $r_0\cosh(c\tau/r_0)$
Period of $l$, a length; each event is identified with its images under a boost of rapidity $\beta/r_0$

coordinates.convention: We use coordinates $(\tau, l, \theta, \phi)$, with $\tau$ the proper time since the Cauchy horizon of the observers at rest, and $l$ a length, periodic with period $\beta$. We take components in the chart $x^0 = c\tau$, and a dot in the geodesic equations is a derivative with respect to an affine parameter, so $\dot{\tau}$ means $d(c\tau)/d\lambda$.

coordinates.name: Steady state
domains: (\tau, x, y, z) \sim (\tau + \beta/c, e^{-\beta/r_0}x, e^{-\beta/r_0}y, e^{-\beta/r_0}z)\;\text{(the boost)}

parameters.description: De Sitter radius, a length, fixed by the cosmological constant $\Lambda$ through $r_0 = \sqrt{3/\Lambda}$; the expansion rate of the flat slices is $c/r_0$
A length; each event is identified with its images under a boost of rapidity $\beta/r_0$, which shifts $c\tau$ by $\beta$ and shrinks $x$, $y$, and $z$ by $e^{-\beta/r_0}$

coordinates.convention: We use coordinates $(\tau, x, y, z)$, with $\tau$ carrying dimensions of time and $x$, $y$, and $z$ comoving lengths. We take components in the chart $x^0 = c\tau$, and a dot in the geodesic equations is a derivative with respect to an affine parameter, so $\dot{\tau}$ means $d(c\tau)/d\lambda$.

coordinates.name: Conformal

parameters.description: De Sitter radius, a length, fixed by the cosmological constant $\Lambda$ through $r_0 = \sqrt{3/\Lambda}$; future infinity lies at $\eta = 0$
A length; each event is identified with its images under a boost of rapidity $\beta/r_0$, which shrinks $\eta$ and $\rho$ by $e^{-\beta/r_0}$

coordinates.convention: We use coordinates $(\eta, \rho, \theta, \phi)$, with the conformal time $\eta = -r_0e^{-c\tau/r_0}$ of the steady state chart a negative length and $\rho = \sqrt{x^2 + y^2 + z^2}$ its comoving radius. No coordinate carries dimensions of time, and a dot in the geodesic equations is a derivative with respect to an affine parameter.
